title: Why Heat Pumps are now leaving people COLD
summary: A New England installer says heat pumps run to 0°F and below but lose efficiency and capacity under about 20-30°F, so older homes in cold climates need supplemental heat such as heat strips.

assertions.quote: heat pumps cannot work in cold climates now that is absolutely false
many of them now include a function called hyper heat that can allow a heat pump to effectively operate down to -20°
they can still generate heat but they become much less efficient now efficiency just means that your electric bill is going to get higher
when the temperature goes below about 30° the efficiency drops way down that means your electric bill is going to begin to Skyrocket
if you've got a house that's 15 years or older you are definitely going to experience problems
it is much less electricity than just simply running your heat pump endlessly trying to make up a temperature

verdicts.note: Resistance strips have a COP of 1, so any heat the running heat pump can still supply costs less than the same heat from strips.

The report says excessive auxiliary resistance runtime is costly and significant energy waste, to be minimized by proper heat pump sizing and controls (elsewhere it notes the auxiliary heater runs at COP 1).

When the heat pump could not catch up quickly after a setpoint change it brought on auxiliary heat, which the report says is less efficient and raises energy use and cost; it recommends avoiding such calls.
RMI's modelled heat pumps cool at SEER 18 against SEER 16 for a new AC, and it says they often cool much more efficiently than existing AC systems (a modelling assumption).
Heat pumps can cool as efficiently as central air conditioning and more efficiently than window or portable units (a secondary citation to Carrier and BC Hydro).
